meta.title: ENG-4238 — Agentic editing, sliced from the net diff
meta.subtitle: Partitioning main → codex/edit-mode into a layerable PR stack.
intro: The branch hardens the str_replace_editor agentic-edit pipeline in lib/text-engine/: how a staged edit is located in a live rich-text editor, highlighted for preview, and pasted over on accept — plus how editors are addressed, and the gate that turns it on.
Target: a fresh ENG-4238 worktree. Apply the slices in order, each its own PR; build + test + review one, then add the next. Combined they equal the branch tip exactly.
meta.principle: The only input is the final net diff (git diff main..HEAD). Every slice is a subset of that diff's hunks; the union of all slices is the diff. Slices are ordered so each compiles and tests green stacked on the previous. We do not reconstruct development history — work added and removed inside the branch never appears in the net diff, so it is not a slice.

excluded.title: transient resolve state
excluded.reason: added then deleted mid-branch. End-state UnresolvedReason = "editor-gone" | "stale" | "no-seed". No "remove transient" work exists to slice.

excluded.title: "method A" whole-document alignment / its removal
excluded.reason: the end state simply is windowed alignment with a cell-count cap as a backstop; both coexist in the final code. No net removal, so no "precise-highlight fix" slice.

excluded.title: reverse-highlight
excluded.reason: added then deleted. Nothing in the net diff.

sections.net: The in-memory editor registry (editable_node_index.ts + its WeakRef e-N map) is gone. Editors are addressed by an e--prefixed reference id from the existing FNV-hash family (siblings: l- links, i- inputs), resolved statelessly.
sections.design: Resolution reuses the form-fill path: resolveElementByFingerprint runs a fresh input-discovery pass and calls findTargetCandidate. Duplicate fingerprints are non-addressable (ambiguous → null). The tab resource surfaces each contenteditable as a [label][e-…] marker.
sections.layering: The registry is consumed by resolve-edit and read-editor; deleting it forces the addressing swap at every site in one slice. Everything downstream resolves editors this way.
sections.verify: DOM discovery/resolution unit tests; resource-renderer snapshot tests for the [e-…] markers; tool-contract tests. Feature still gated.

slices.title: Ancestor-scoped selection muting
slices.unblocks: flash-free live verification of later slices

sections.net: When the engine programmatically selects an editor to copy/read, the marker that suppresses the visible blue selection is placed on the editable's ancestor rather than the editable element itself.
sections.design: Editors like CKEditor rewrite attributes on their editable node, stripping a marker placed there. Marking one level up survives that rewrite, so the selection-suppression CSS keeps matching and the user sees no flash.
sections.verify: Unit test asserts the marker lands on the ancestor and survives a simulated editable rewrite. Live: read/highlight on CKEditor shows no blue flash.

sections.net: Two new pure modules + tests: text-dom-utils.ts (shared primitives) and source-mapped-display.ts (projection engine). Exported and exposed on the devtools bundle. No live caller yet.
sections.design: text-dom-utils: visible-text extraction, zero-width stripping, change-core diffing, lane type, and changedVisibleSpan (one function → both highlight and dim spans). source-mapped-display: plain-lane exact character-aligned projection; html-lane bounded-window alignment (±300 chars) with a cell-count cap backstop and code-unit offset indexing for astral chars.
sections.layering: New files compile with no consumer; the resolve pipeline (Slice 4) imports them. Landing the engine first keeps Slice 4 a focused wiring change.
sections.verify: Unit tests drive projection and span functions directly. Exercise live via the devtools bundle.

slices.title: Resolve / apply pipeline + workspace
slices.unblocks: the preview/accept flow works end-to-end (still gated)

sections.net: resolve-edit.ts is rewritten into the live locate/apply orchestration that consumes the engine, and ChatWorkspace.tsx consumes its result. The fuzzy matcher (approx-string-match) is deleted — resolve-edit was its last caller.
sections.design:
• Staleness rides the live DOM (oldContentPresentInLiveDom) — the clipboard can lag, the DOM can't.
  • Clipboard is subordinate: fixes only the lane, feeds display, provides the apply splice target.
  • Locate = anchor (walk up) then narrow (walk down) to the splice target.
  • Outcomes are total: resolved, or one of three terminal reasons; apply reports retryable paste-failed vs stale.
  • One span feeds page highlight + iframe dim.
sections.layering: The pipeline and its sole UI consumer are compile-coupled through ResolveResult, so they land together. They require fingerprint addressing (1) and the engine (3).
sections.verify: Locate/apply tests over the public surface; a stale clipboard with old_content still in the DOM resolves rather than dismissing. Live: fast-cycle highlights, accept an edit.

sections.net: Pure subtraction: word-diff (already dead in main) and its test deleted; unused text-engine constants and selection helpers trimmed; the content-script narrows from a whole-barrel import to direct module imports.
sections.design: No behavior change. Genuinely-defensive guards and the retry/fallback paths from Slice 4 are kept.
sections.verify: Type-check + lint + both bundle builds stay green; consumer census confirms nothing removed still has a live reader.

sections.net: The read_editor_rich_text and str_replace_editor worker modules are registered in the default tool set, and the system prompt routes edits to them.
sections.design: Routing: revise existing text → read then str_replace with the e- id; add new text → propose_insert; set discrete fields → propose_input_modification. Strictly last so the gate opens only once the logic beneath it is verified.
sections.verify: Chat-session tests assert the tools are advertised and the prompt routes correctly. Live end-to-end: ask the agent to revise existing editor text → a str_replace_editor card.
